stories.title: Anthony Henry to undergo neck surgery and face months of recovery
stories.tldr: AEW wrestler Anthony Henry has announced he must undergo surgery for a herniated disc that is pressing directly on his spinal cord. The WorkHorsemen star, who has not wrestled since July, shared that his recovery is expected to take between three to six months. Despite the scary nature of the spinal injury, Henry remains optimistic and plans to return to the ring stronger than ever.

stories.title: Former WWE star KAIRI announced for Chris Jericho's Rock 'N' Wrestling Rager at Sea
stories.tldr: Former WWE star KAIRI has been announced for the upcoming Chris Jericho Rock N Wrestling Rager at Sea cruise taking place from November 7-11. KAIRI, who has been a free agent since her release from WWE in April, is scheduled to participate in meet and greets, photo sessions, and overall cruise festivities. Her booking has fueled heavy speculation regarding a potential future with All Elite Wrestling, especially since the cruise will feature a live episode of AEW Collision. However, observers note that the cruise lineup also includes talent from TNA and other promotions, meaning her appearance does not guarantee an imminent AEW debut.

stories.title: Chris Jericho says AEW no longer needs to actively recruit wrestlers
stories.tldr: Chris Jericho recently reflected on the early days of AEW, detailing how he personally helped recruit top stars like Jon Moxley and PAC to the fledgling promotion. He noted that while PAC initially hesitated out of loyalty to Dragon Gate, he eventually joined the company. Jericho explained that AEW has now grown to a point where active recruitment is no longer necessary because wrestlers naturally want to come based on its strong reputation. He also touched on AEW's alternative corporate structure compared to WWE and promoted his upcoming match against Nick Wayne.

stories.title: Bryan & Vinny review AEW Grand Slam France and WWE NXT
stories.tldr: The latest episode of The Bryan & Vinny Show covers a packed slate of professional wrestling action, highlighted by a strong edition of AEW Grand Slam France featuring a main event clash between Will Ospreay and Kazuchika Okada. The hosts also dive deep into the recent WWE NXT television episode, which closed out with a memorable women's battle royal main event. According to the review, this chaotic match truly needs to be seen to be believed due to its wild combination of in-ring action, questionable booking, and unique commentary.

stories.title: Dustin Rhodes continues pizza war with review of New Jersey slice
stories.tldr: Dustin Rhodes has expanded his passionate online pizza war by taking direct aim at New Jersey style slices, calling them disgusting and greasy. The AEW veteran has spent weeks trashing New York pizza, condemning popular toppings like olives, pickles, and pineapple, and even labeling vegetables as demonic. While he fiercely rejects regional styles from New York and the Jersey Shore, Rhodes maintains that New Haven Tavern style is the ultimate superior choice.

stories.title: Jim Ross advises Aleister Black to get promotion promises in writing
stories.tldr: Hall of Fame broadcaster Jim Ross recently weighed in on Aleister Black discussing unfulfilled expectations during his WWE return. Drawing from his extensive experience as a former head of talent relations, Ross advised that wrestlers should secure any verbal promises by having them formally added to their contracts as written addendums. Additionally, Ross cautioned Black to steer clear of ongoing backstage drama to ensure prospective employers do not view him as a difficult talent to work with. Despite these concerns, Ross praised Black's overall in-ring ability and appearance, expressing confidence that the star will easily find his next major opportunity.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite October 6 viewership numbers
stories.tldr: AEW Dynamite experienced a sharp week-over-week decline on October 6, 2026, pulling in 495,000 viewers and a 0.11 demo rating on TBS compared to the previous week's 899,000 viewers and 0.22 rating. Despite this steep drop from late September, the numbers still reflect a positive year-over-year increase when compared to the same week in October 2025. These figures account strictly for linear television broadcasts on TBS and exclude any digital or streaming metrics.

stories.title: Potential AEW opponents for Jon Moxley
stories.tldr: Despite facing nearly everyone on the roster and holding the record for the most wins in AEW history, Death Riders leader Jon Moxley still has a few fresh matchups left to make. This feature explores five potential first-time opponents for Moxley, including former WWE stars and international talents. The list highlights high-profile names who could step up to challenge Moxley and showcase their singles abilities in the company.

stories.title: Jim Ross recalls Jake Hager's Oklahoma roots after Power Slap eye injury
stories.tldr: Wrestling legend Jim Ross recently shared personal memories of former WWE star Jake Hager while reacting to Hager's recent Power Slap eye injury. Ross highlighted Hager's impressive athletic background in Oklahoma, including his time as an All-American wrestler and football player at the University of Oklahoma. While unsure of Hager's exact motivations for entering the slap-fighting league, Ross expressed hope that the move was driven by either a strong payday or a deep passion for physical competition.

stories.title: AEW Blood & Guts 2026 match lineup speculation
stories.tldr: With AEW Blood & Guts approaching in four weeks in Jacksonville, Florida, the current storylines may not quite be at natural blood feud levels yet. The author explores potential faction warfare for both the men and women divisions, including the possibility of a three-way WarGames match or outside-the-box team combinations. Ultimately, the writer proposes specific dream lineups for both men and women inside the double-ring steel cage to spark fan discussion.

stories.title: Josh Alexander reflects on wrestling Bryan Danielson on AEW PAC tribute show
stories.tldr: Josh Alexander recently opened up about his emotional experience wrestling alongside Bryan Danielson during a special AEW tribute show dedicated to Pac. Alexander recalled how Danielson personally surprised him backstage with the news that they would be part of the main event match against The Don Callis Family. Although the locker room was grieving the recent losses of Pac and Andy Williams, Alexander found the opportunity to perform to be a cathartic way to honor their memories. Ultimately, the poignant evening reminded Alexander to cherish his peers, take more photos with loved ones, and express his appreciation for them.

stories.title: The Young Bucks pay tribute to PAC
stories.tldr: The Young Bucks paid an emotional tribute to their longtime friend PAC following a dedicated AEW Dynamite tribute show. Speaking on their Being The Elite vlog, Matt and Nick Jackson reflected on their two-decade friendship with PAC, which began when he took care of them during their first trip to Japan in 2008. Matt became visibly emotional recalling a recent conversation where PAC noted they would both be 60 in another twenty years, heartbroken that his friend will never reach that age. The brothers shared memories of rooming together in Japan, working in PWG, and how PAC had previously advised them against joining WWE.

stories.title: Jim Ross discusses benefits of Chris Jericho cruise for wrestlers' families
stories.tldr: AEW commentator Jim Ross recently praised Chris Jericho's wrestling cruises during an episode of Grilling JR with Conrad Thompson. Ross highlighted how the unique vacation and wrestling events allow performers to travel with their significant others and spend quality time together away from their usual hectic schedules. He also discussed the logistics of potentially staging an episode of Collision aboard the ship while it is docked.

stories.title: Comparing WWE's product style to AEW's target audience
stories.tldr: Conrad Thompson recently sparked discussion by claiming AEW makes wrestling for fans while WWE makes it for investors, a sentiment previously echoed by figures like Tony Khan and Ricochet. An analysis of this claim compares the two major promotions to distinct movie genres to better understand their business and creative models. WWE is likened to the blockbuster superhero genre aimed at entertaining a broad, casual audience, whereas AEW is compared to independent horror films catering specifically to hardcore wrestling enthusiasts. Ultimately, the piece concludes that both companies serve different segments of the fanbase effectively, and catering to casuals or shareholders does not mean WWE is not also creating a product for wrestling fans.

stories.title: Jeff Jarrett praises depth of AEW roster for high-quality PPV shows
stories.tldr: Jeff Jarrett recently discussed the high quality of All Elite Wrestling pay-per-view events on his My World podcast with host Conrad Thompson. Jarrett explained that the promotion's impressive roster depth is the single biggest factor behind these successful shows, even allowing for stronger critical reception compared to weekly television. By combining the talent pools of both AEW and Ring of Honor, Tony Khan can leave top stars off a card so they return feeling fresh for the next event. Jarrett compared this strategic advantage to a successful NFL franchise that relies on strong backups at every position.

stories.title: AEW WrestleDream 2026 ticket sales update
stories.tldr: AEW WrestleDream 2026 is scheduled for Saturday, October 17 at the Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida, with current ticket distribution standing at 4,497 according to WrestleTix. While this marks an increase of 245 tickets over the past week and outperforms AEW's January 2026 Dynamite event in the same venue, the show currently trails last year's WrestleDream total of 6,293 by just over 2,000 tickets. Fans still looking to attend can find standard admission tickets starting at $36.40, alongside approximately 162 tickets currently available on the resale market. To drive sales ahead of the event, AEW has announced a loaded card featuring several high-profile championship matches and a chaotic multi-person main event.

stories.title: AEW WrestleDream 2026 match card developments
stories.tldr: Three new matches are projected to join the AEW WrestleDream 2026 card on October 17 in Orlando. The additions feature Andrade El Idolo defending the National Championship against Tommaso Ciampa, The Brawling Birds putting the Women's World Tag Team Titles on the line against Harley Cameron and Kris Statlander, and Kazuchika Okada defending the International Championship against Daniel Garcia.

stories.title: Swerve Strickland and wrestling world react to the passing of PAC
stories.tldr: The wrestling world continues to mourn the sudden passing of Benjamin Satterley, known to fans as PAC or Neville, who tragically died at the age of 40. AEW star Swerve Strickland recently opened up about how the locker room is processing their grief through open communication and sharing fond memories of their peer. Meanwhile, a newly released 40-minute tribute video from his former colleagues features emotional stories and heartfelt tributes from stars like Kevin Owens, Sami Zayn, Finn Balor, and William Regal. Additionally, newly surfaced 911 audio and police reports have provided heartbreaking details regarding the final moments before first responders arrived.

stories.title: MJF makes surprise NJPW appearance and issues challenge
stories.tldr: AEW star MJF made a surprise pre-taped appearance during NJPW Road to King of Pro Wrestling to issue a bold challenge to G1 Climax winner Ryohei Oiwa. MJF offered to put his self-proclaimed real AEW World Championship on the line while vowing to prove he is the true king of the headlock takeover. Alongside the challenge, MJF trash-talked New Japan, calling it a second-rate company and a blight on society in an effort to lock the Forbidden Door for good. As Oiwa prepares for his major IWGP Heavyweight Championship match against Yota Tsuji this coming Monday, fans are left speculating about a potential confrontation with the American star.

stories.title: CMLL announces AEW representatives for the 2026 Women's Grand Prix
stories.tldr: CMLL has officially announced the full participant list and AEW representatives for the upcoming 2026 Women's Grand Prix, which takes place on October 23 at Arena Mexico. AEW is sending Queen Aminata from Guinea, Megan Bayne from the United States, and Harley Cameron from Australia to compete in the prestigious international tournament. The stacked field features top talent representing countries from around the globe, including Japan, the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom, Canada, and Mexico. Current CMLL World Women's Champion Persephone, who won the 2025 tournament, will lead Team Mexico in the defense of her home turf.

stories.title: Chris Jericho addresses potential WWE Hall of Fame induction
stories.tldr: AEW star Chris Jericho recently addressed the possibility of eventually entering the WWE Hall of Fame during an interview. He firmly believes his nearly two-decade career in WWE generated enough memorable moments, matches, and rivalries to warrant an induction. However, he acknowledges that industry politics and his current active status with AEW might complicate or delay the process. Ultimately, Jericho is unconcerned with official corporate recognition, noting that he considers himself already inducted in the minds of fans and in his own head.

stories.title: Kofi comments on ROH World Title loss to Bandido at AEW Dynamite Grand Slam Paris
stories.tldr: Kofi recently challenged Bandido for the ROH World Championship at AEW Dynamite Grand Slam Paris but ultimately came up short. Despite missing out on his first piece of singles gold in the promotion, Kofi expressed gratitude for the passionate French crowd and shared high praise for the champion on social media. He will soon have a chance at redemption when he defends his trios title against Bandido and his allies at WrestleDream. Bandido's victory marked another milestone in a historic championship reign that is closing in on major company records.

stories.title: NJPW stars expected to appear on AEW programming
stories.tldr: The working relationship between All Elite Wrestling and New Japan Pro-Wrestling is heating up again, with AEW star MJF issuing a direct challenge to NJPW standout Ryohei Oiwa to step into the ring. As MJF sets his sights on Japan, speculation is growing regarding which other New Japan competitors might cross the forbidden door to appear on Dynamite and Collision, or face MJF in crossover matches. Names like Shota Umino, Callum Newman, and Yota Tsuji are all heavily rumored for upcoming high-profile programs intersecting with AEW talent as major events like King of Pro-Wrestling and Wrestle Kingdom approach.

stories.title: MJF issues statement on working with New Japan Pro-Wrestling
stories.tldr: AEW star MJF has shocked the wrestling world by officially challenging NJPW G1 Climax winner Ryohei Oiwa, despite years of criticizing New Japan as a second-rate company. In a statement to Fightful and a video message at a New Japan event, MJF stated his goals are to prove NJPW isn't a real company, establish himself as the master of the headlock, and upset Puro Twitter. Furthermore, MJF has sweetened the challenge by offering his own version of the AEW World Title, reigniting his long-running disdain for NJPW as Oiwa prepares for his upcoming IWGP Heavyweight Championship match.

stories.title: Eric Bischoff comments on PAC tribute show and recent AEW injuries/deaths
stories.tldr: Wrestling veteran Eric Bischoff recently addressed several concerning issues within All Elite Wrestling on his podcast, starting with the tragic back-to-back deaths of Andy Williams and PAC. Bischoff called the passing of two wrestlers in their early forties unnatural, warning that it feels concerningly reminiscent of the frequent deaths seen in the industry during the 1990s and early 2000s. In addition to these tragedies, Bischoff strongly criticized AEW management and veterans for rushing Steven Borden, the son of Sting, onto television too early in his career. He argued that Borden lacked the necessary in-ring experience for dangerous high spots, ultimately resulting in a head injury at the All Out pay-per-view that could jeopardize his future in the business.

stories.title: Ryohei Oiwa responds to MJF's AEW World Title challenge
stories.tldr: NJPW star Ryohei Oiwa has responded to a challenge from MJF for an inter-promotional match involving MJF's custom Triple B championship. However, Oiwa has made it clear that his immediate priority is his upcoming IWGP Heavyweight Championship match against Yota Tsuji at King of Pro-Wrestling following his 2026 G1 Climax victory. MJF has indicated he is willing to wait for Oiwa while continuing to mock New Japan Pro-Wrestling and troll fans on social media.

stories.title: Daily Update: New John Cena movie role, MJF, Yuto-Ice
stories.tldr: The latest wrestling news update covers major developments including Cody Rhodes re-signing with WWE and John Cena landing a new comedy-thriller film role alongside David Harbour. The Wrestling Observer Newsletter highlights a touching tribute to the late Benjamin Pac Satterley alongside extensive coverage of recent pay-per-views and industry news. In other updates, MJF explains his controversial statements regarding New Japan Pro Wrestling, and Wren Sinclair punches her ticket to Halloween Havoc. Additional coverage spans injury updates on Jim Ross, backstage rumors regarding Sheamus, and extensive media appearances by WWE talent ahead of upcoming events.

stories.title: Big Vinny V: Why next week’s Monday Night Raw is so important for the 946
stories.tldr: Next week on Monday Night Raw, the newly formed group known as the 946 faces a crucial sink-or-swim test against the dominant Bloodline. While veteran Keys brings significant pay-per-view experience to the table, partners Bronco Nima and Lucien Price have very limited televised history with opponents Solo Sikoa and the Usos. Because many fans will be seeing Nima and Price for the very first time, making a strong initial impression is vital. Ultimately, the stable must prove immediately that they can operate at a main event level against WWEs premier modern faction.

stories.title: Bryan Alvarez’s AEW Dynamite October 6, 2026 report
stories.tldr: Bryan Alvarez has released his detailed report covering the October 6, 2026 episode of AEW Dynamite. The subscriber-exclusive breakdown offers behind the scenes notes and analysis on the matches and segments that aired during the broadcast. Fans of the audio update can now access the full report through the standard subscription platform.

stories.title: Jim Ross undergoes brain surgery and provides health updates
stories.tldr: AEW commentator Jim Ross has successfully undergone his second brain surgery to address complications with his brain shunt. Following a CT scan that revealed bleeding, doctors performed the corrective procedure on Wednesday morning. Ross is currently in recovery and expected to return home later today as he continues managing his ongoing health challenges.

stories.title: Samoa Joe qualifies for Clockwork Carnage at AEW WrestleDream over Jack Perry
stories.tldr: Samoa Joe secured his spot in the upcoming AEW WrestleDream Clockwork Carnage match by defeating Jack Perry at Grand Slam France using a decisive Muscle Buster. The high-stakes qualifier marked Joe's triumphant in-ring return following a nearly five-month absence. Meanwhile, Perry's ongoing quest to defeat every former AEW World Champion continues to hit roadblocks, adding to a troubling trend of high-profile losses against the company's elite.

stories.title: The future of Clockwork Carnage after AEW WrestleDream
stories.tldr: Following Will Ospreay's introduction of the Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW World Championship, full rules for the eight-person, two-stage bout have been revealed. The unique structure combines a staggered entry elimination format with a final fifteen-minute scoring period reminiscent of NXT's Iron Survivor challenge. If successful at WrestleDream, Tony Khan could potentially add the concept to AEW's permanent annual calendar alongside staples like Blood and Guts. Meanwhile, speculation is already swirling regarding potential future challengers and successors to Ospreay's throne, including Samoa Joe, Darby Allin, Andrade El Idolo, and MJF.

stories.title: Chris Jericho's future plans and role in AEW
stories.tldr: Chris Jericho is cementing his role as an AEW mentor by prioritizing the elevation of younger talent over his own championship pursuits and win-loss record. His current focus centers on a high-profile feud with 21-year-old Nick Wayne, culminating on AEW Collision. While he occasionally needs a victory to keep stories compelling, Jericho's primary goal is helping rising stars unlock their potential and drive the company forward.

stories.title: Sheamus Free Agency and AEW Interest Rumors
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Sheamus officially became a free agent in early October after declining a restructured contract that involved a significant pay cut, ending a nearly two-decade run with the company. While he has not yet entered substantial contract discussions with All Elite Wrestling, several prominent veterans and former colleagues within the promotion are actively pushing management to sign him. In addition to AEW, other organizations such as TNA have shown interest in securing the services of the decorated veteran, leaving his next career move entirely open as he evaluates his options.

stories.title: Will Ospreay Feuds and Title Reign Analysis
stories.tldr: Will Ospreay is using his AEW World Championship reign to introduce a competitive, sports-based presentation inspired by boxing and the World Cup, aiming to bring innovative concept matches like the Clockwork Carnage match to the company. His tenure is deeply rooted in history, with past and future feuds involving long-standing rivals like Kazuchika Okada, Jon Moxley, Ricochet, and Kyle Fletcher. Additionally, Ospreay's ongoing back-and-forth between AEW and NJPW has set up potential title contenders from New Japan, including Yuto-Ice, OSKAR, Zack Sabre Jr., Jeff Cobb, and Callum Newman. Through these carefully crafted rivalries and main event matches, Ospreay seeks to shape the future direction of professional wrestling.

stories.title: Rush Comments on AEW Absence
stories.tldr: AEW star Rush has provided an update on his ongoing absence from television, suggesting to fans that he might not return until next year. The former La Facción Ingobernable member has not wrestled on AEW programming since a squash match on Collision in early July. Despite internet speculation regarding his health or potential moves to other promotions like WWE or AAA, Rush has clarified that he is entirely healthy, not complaining, and simply enjoying time with his family.

stories.title: Tony Khan Responds to ROH Criticism
stories.tldr: AEW and Ring of Honor President Tony Khan recently defended his promotion on social media after a fan labeled the product an absolute disaster. Khan argued that the criticism relied on outdated television from July while ignoring recent successes like the August Death Before Dishonor pay-per-view and free YouTube broadcasts. In separate wrestling media news, Vince Russo and Jonathan Coachman announced plans to launch a new collaborative show on November 1 that will explore Coachman's college basketball career and personal background.

stories.title: Jim Ross Comments on Kevin Owens and AEW
stories.tldr: Wrestling legend Jim Ross recently discussed Kevin Owens on his podcast, noting that the WWE star could easily have been a world champion in AEW. While Ross praised Owens as a versatile and reliable locker room leader, he acknowledged that WWE has taken good care of him during recent injuries. Even so, Ross believes it is not too late for Owens to eventually jump to AEW and would welcome him with open arms. However, despite this potential interest, Ross ultimately suspects that Owens has already re-signed with WWE, where he remains a prominent fixture at age forty-two.

stories.title: AEW Targeting Indie Wrestler Xanti Li
stories.tldr: AEW and Ring of Honor are reportedly showing strong mutual interest in signing indie wrestler Xanti Li following an impressive debut appearance. Trained by former WWE stars Shawn Spears and Tyler Breeze at Flatbacks Wrestling School, Li has quickly made waves despite starting her career in August 2025. While no official contract has been finalized yet, she is expected to continue making appearances on Ring of Honor programming as both sides evaluate a potential future partnership.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite Global Search Interest
stories.tldr: Google search interest for AEW Dynamite is up twenty percent globally year on year, driven primarily by a massive one hundred percent increase in Mexico. Meanwhile, domestic growth remains more modest with a five percent rise in the United States and two percent in the United Kingdom. Data from Mexico reveals four major search interest spikes throughout the year that align with key events, major matches, and the ongoing talent exchange with CMLL. While WWE remains the dominant household name in the region, AEW's strategic partnerships and crossover appearances by stars like Mistico and PAC have noticeably boosted international brand awareness.

stories.title: Tony Khan Fires Back At Fan Criticism Of Current ROH Product
stories.tldr: AEW and ROH President Tony Khan recently defended Ring of Honor against a fan on social media who labeled the current product an absolute disaster. Khan argued that the critic was unfairly judging the promotion by using an outdated television episode from July rather than looking at recent output. To support his defense, Khan pointed to the widely praised Death Before Dishonor pay-per-view in August and a recent free episode on YouTube featuring tremendous action.

stories.title: New developments ahead of NJPW King of Pro Wrestling 2026
stories.tldr: The Knockout Brothers captured the IWGP Tag Team Championships by defeating United Empire at a recent Road to King of Pro Wrestling event. Following their victory, Yuto-Ice and OSKAR revealed that former United Empire member Jeff Cobb will be their mystery partner. They will challenge HENARE, Great-O-Khan, and Will Ospreay for the NEVER Openweight Tag Team titles at Sumo Hall. The big event takes place on Monday and will air live on NJPW World with English commentary.

stories.title: First AEW Grand Slam France Collision match announced
stories.tldr: A high profile match originally planned for the AEW Grand Slam France edition of Dynamite has been shifted to the upcoming Saturday Collision broadcast instead. AEW announced that the Chris Jericho versus Nick Wayne rematch will take place at the Adidas Arena in Paris and air on Saturday after being taped following Tuesday's Dynamite. This bout serves as a sequel to their September 16 encounter where Jericho emerged victorious only to be laid out by Wayne using a rope assisted low blow. The rest of the Saturday Collision lineup is set to be revealed later on Tuesday.

stories.title: AEW WrestleDream and Grand Slam France Match Cards and Results
stories.tldr: Following Grand Slam France, several major matches and title bouts have been locked in for AEW WrestleDream. Will Ospreay successfully defended his world title against Kazuchika Okada and established the rules for the upcoming Clockwork Carnage match, where Samoa Joe has earned the first qualifying spot. Additional WrestleDream card updates feature Jon Moxley defending the Continental Championship against Mark Davis and a two-out-of-three falls trios title match.

stories.title: Eric Bischoff and QT Marshall Dispute Over Steven Borden Injury
stories.tldr: Eric Bischoff recently criticized AEW on his podcast for letting an inexperienced Steven Borden perform risky maneuvers during his recent pay-per-view match. AEW executive QT Marshall fired back by defending Borden's extensive training regimen that has been ongoing since 2024. Meanwhile, backstage updates indicate that Borden is currently doing well and is not experiencing any headaches or dizziness.

stories.title: Skydance Acquisition of WBD and Tony Khan Reaction
stories.tldr: The 110 billion dollar Paramount Skydance acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery is officially complete, saddling the new corporate giant with 80 billion dollars in debt. AEW President Tony Khan publicly praised the merger on social media, expressing excitement about working under Skydance CEO David Ellison. Khan delivered his remarks from Paris ahead of the AEW Grand Slam France broadcast, marking the company's first event under the new corporate banner.

stories.title: AEW Discussed Elimination Chamber-Style Match
stories.tldr: Before booking the newly announced Clockwork Carnage match, AEW creative discussed a six-person gimmick structure inspired by WWE's Elimination Chamber that was ultimately shelved. Tony Khan has added format tweaks to Will Ospreay's brainchild, including qualifying matches that begin on Dynamite. The inaugural eight-man bout will feature staggered entries leading into a 15-minute Iron Man finish at WrestleDream.

stories.title: Enzo Amore Clarifies AEW Criticism, Takes Issue With Timing Of Maven Interview
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Enzo Amore recently sparked backlash after a resurfaced interview showed him blasting AEW for letting backstage altercations leak to the public. Amore has now clarified that the conversation actually took place months ago, taking serious issue with Maven Huffman for timing the release right after a heartfelt tribute show for PAC. Maven's production team defended the rollout by explaining that the footage was shelved for over a year before finally being published due to fan demand and a shorter run time.

stories.title: Enzo Amore comments on AEW locker room and Maven interview
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Enzo Amore recently criticized AEW's locker room culture during a resurfaced interview with Maven Huffman, blasting the promotion for letting backstage altercations leak publicly. Amore contrasted this with his time in WWE, where he claimed physical fights and management discussions were kept strictly private. Following the video's release, Amore took to social media to express frustration over the timing, noting it was filmed in early 2025 and surfaced shortly after AEW held a tribute show for his late friend, PAC. Maven later explained that the footage had originally been shelved after Amore requested a portion be cut, but was ultimately published due to fan demand for extra content.

stories.title: Jon Moxley and Gabe Kidd tag team match at AEW Grand Slam France
stories.tldr: AEW President Tony Khan has officially added a high-profile tag team match to the upcoming AEW Grand Slam France event in Paris, featuring Death Riders members Jon Moxley and Gabe Kidd. The bout was booked following a challenge from the Don Callis Family's Mark Davis and Jake Doyle in the wake of Moxley's recent match against Doyle. Despite some previous tension between Moxley and Kidd, the uneasy alliance will now square off against Davis and Doyle at the Adidas Arena.

stories.title: Bryan Danielson AEW plans following in-ring return
stories.tldr: Bryan Danielson made a surprise in-ring return during a special AEW Dynamite tribute show dedicated to the late PAC. He teamed up with the Death Riders to defeat the Don Callis family, bringing closure to his past rivalry with Jon Moxley. Despite this emotional comeback, backstage reports indicate that Danielson is not returning to full-time action or regular television plans. His appearance was strictly a one-night-only exception made specifically to honor PAC.

stories.title: New police report details regarding PAC's passing
stories.tldr: A newly released police incident report sheds light on the final hours of AEW star PAC, who was found unresponsive in a vehicle near Chicago O Hare International Airport on September 27. Authorities found his phone open to airport directions and answered a call from a woman who confirmed he had planned to grab lunch before a delayed flight to the United Kingdom. Although an initial autopsy has been performed, his official cause of death remains pending further testing while the global wrestling community continues to honor his memory.

stories.title: Chris Jericho says he doesn't have to win ever again in AEW
stories.tldr: During an appearance on TMZ's Inside The Ring podcast, Chris Jericho stated that wins and losses are no longer a priority for him in AEW as he focuses on elevating younger talent. He pointed to past extended programs and matches with stars like MJF, Will Ospreay, and Bandido as examples of how working with him helped launch or solidify their main event status. While he acknowledged that he still needs to win occasionally to keep stories compelling, his primary goal now is delivering great performances and helping emerging wrestlers find their potential.

stories.title: AEW locker room reaction to PAC tribute show
stories.tldr: Following the passing of PAC, AEW recently hosted a heartfelt tribute episode of Dynamite to honor his legacy. Backstage, the emotional atmosphere culminated with the entire locker room sitting and crying together after watching the closing tribute video. Will Ospreay and Ricochet delivered a critically acclaimed and intensely difficult singles match on the card, with Ospreay even dusting off the Black Arrow for the first time in eight years. Reflecting on the heavy night, Mike Bailey and Ospreay both shared insights into the raw emotions and immense physical toll required to properly honor their late friend.

stories.title: Adam Copeland bucket list venue and WWE departure
stories.tldr: Adam Copeland recently reflected on his decision to leave WWE for AEW, noting that the move allowed him to check off several historic wrestling venues from his career bucket list. Over the past month, the WWE Hall of Famer has wrestled at Arena Mexico, Wembley Stadium, and the Mattamy Athletic Centre, which sits on the historic grounds of Maple Leaf Gardens in his hometown of Toronto. Industry reports indicate that Copeland still has one major venue left on his list: the Tokyo Dome, with speculation pointing toward a possible appearance at Wrestle Kingdom in January 2027. Copeland credited AEW President Tony Khan for fostering an environment that makes these unique career opportunities possible.

stories.title: Jeff Jarrett discusses unfinished AEW story with MJF
stories.tldr: Jeff Jarrett recently discussed his career goals in wrestling, noting an unfinished storyline with MJF and his desire to eventually chase tag or trios gold. He also shared high praise for Bryan Danielson as one of the greatest in-ring storytellers of all time. In addition, Jarrett emotionally recalled his final backstage conversation with Pac at AEW All Out, just a day before the star's sudden and tragic passing.

stories.title: Wheeler Yuta wants AEW World Tag Titles with Death Riders
stories.tldr: Wheeler Yuta recently expressed his desire to pursue the AEW World Tag Team Championships alongside fellow Death Riders associate Daniel Garcia. During an interview with The Wrestling Classic, Yuta highlighted their instant chemistry and shared wrestling philosophies as major reasons to chase tag team gold together. Neither Yuta, Garcia, nor any other member of the Death Riders has ever held the AEW World Tag Team titles. Meanwhile, the current champions, The Young Bucks, are set to defend their titles against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight at the upcoming AEW WrestleDream pay-per-view.

stories.title: Thekla recalls Jeff Jarrett compliment in AEW
stories.tldr: AEW star Thekla recently discussed her chaotic character and memorable moments during a recent interview. She recalled how veteran Jeff Jarrett praised her unhinged behavior with a humorous compliment following her dramatic return promo at All In in London. Meanwhile, fellow veteran Paul Wight had a much more cautious reaction to her antics at the commentary desk, worrying more about spilled drinks than the danger.

stories.title: AEW babyface turns coming soon ahead of WrestleDream
stories.tldr: As AEW approaches the WrestleDream pay-per-view, fan reactions are pushing several prominent heels toward inevitable babyface turns. The Death Riders are positioned to officially transition into fan favorites following a poignant tribute to the late PAC and an alliance with Bryan Danielson. Meanwhile, crowd support for Tommaso Ciampa and growing hostility toward Mercedes Mone in Thekla's upcoming title chase create ideal conditions for both stars to embrace anti-hero roles.

stories.title: Jacques Rougeau disputes report about AEW backstage incident
stories.tldr: Wrestling legend Jacques Rougeau has strongly denied reports that he threw a tantrum backstage at AEW Redemption after a family tribute video was pulled from the broadcast. According to initial reports, the video could not be aired due to unauthorized copyrighted material and AI-generated content discovered at the last minute. However, Rougeau disputed this, stating the video had been approved six weeks prior and that he merely expressed frustration without raising his voice. Ultimately, Rougeau accepted the decision, proceeded with the live segment, and reported having a positive interaction with AEW President Tony Khan afterward.

stories.title: Jim Ross brain procedure and health updates
stories.tldr: AEW announcer Jim Ross is heading back into surgery to address ongoing complications with his brain shunt. Following severe headaches that disrupted his sleep, doctors determined a new procedure was necessary. Additionally, recent medical scans have revealed a concerning spot on his kidney, prompting further testing by his oncology team.

stories.title: Paramount-WBD merger impact on AEW and executive changes
stories.tldr: The upcoming corporate merger will officially close under the Skydance banner on October 6, bringing heavy debt and executive restructuring. TNT Sports CEO Luis Silberwasser is departing, placing AEW under the sports portfolio of incoming executive David Berson. While existing television agreements provide short-term stability, the new leadership faces intense profitability pressures and potential streaming platform consolidation.

stories.title: Tony Khan decisions and changes for AEW PAC tribute show
stories.tldr: Tony Khan made sweeping creative changes to the September 30 episode of Dynamite to ensure it served as a pure tribute to PAC. He completely removed all promotional material and angles for the upcoming pay-per-view and Collision. The original plans for the broadcast were scrapped and delayed to subsequent episodes, forcing the creative team to speed up upcoming storylines as the company prepared for its trip to France.

stories.title: The Rock responds to report about WWE reaction to his AEW praise in PAC tribute
stories.tldr: Dwayne The Rock Johnson has addressed rumors that individuals within WWE were surprised by his public praise of AEW during a video tribute to the late PAC. Following reports that his wording caught some officials off guard, Johnson took to Instagram to clarify his stance. He firmly stated that corporate competition is irrelevant when mourning a member of the wrestling community, emphasizing that humanity and supporting grieving wrestlers matter most to him.

stories.title: Samoa Joe thought his career was over after 2020 concussion
stories.tldr: Samoa Joe recently reflected on a dark period in 2020 when a severe concussion led him to believe his in-ring wrestling career was over. During this time away from the ring, he transitioned to commentary for WWE before experiencing two separate releases due to corporate restructuring. Fortunately, a miraculous turn of events occurred just four hours after his second firing when he received an unexpected call to audition for Peacock's Twisted Metal, ultimately revitalizing his career and leading to his eventual return to professional wrestling with AEW.

stories.title: Jeff Jarrett names his AEW Mount Rushmore with Tony Khan at the top
stories.tldr: Wrestling veteran Jeff Jarrett recently revealed his picks for an AEW Mount Rushmore during an appearance on KickOut, naming Chris Jericho, Sting, The Elite, and MJF as the foundational figures of the company. However, the WWE Hall of Famer emphasized that AEW President Tony Khan belongs in an entirely different category altogether. According to Jarrett, Khan is not merely part of the monument, but is instead the mountain itself whose vision made the entire promotion possible.

stories.title: Alex Zayne Not Under AEW/ROH Contract
stories.tldr: Alex Zayne is currently not under a contract with AEW or ROH despite his regular appearances for the promotion. He recently competed at the Ring of Honor television tapings held at WJCT Studios in Jacksonville, Florida. During these tapings, Zayne faced competitors like Adam Priest and teamed up with Mance Warner.

stories.title: AEW WrestleDream preview and card updates
stories.tldr: AEW is heading toward its WrestleDream pay-per-view in Orlando with plenty of uncertainty surrounding the match card. While three matches have been partially outlined, including a chaotic eight-man Clockwork Carnage match for the World Championship and title defenses for Mercedes Mone and the Young Bucks, several major champions and qualifiers remain up in the air. Upcoming events like Grand Slam France are set to sort out these pivotal challengers before the October pay-per-view.

stories.title: New addition hinted for AEW Death Riders faction
stories.tldr: The AEW Death Riders faction may soon add a female member to help advance their campaign of violence and elevate a new star's career. Three potential candidates for the Jon Moxley led group include Willow Nightingale, Thekla, and Deonna Purrazzo. Each wrestler offers unique possibilities for character evolution, ranging from gritty rebrands to unexpected alliances and dramatic betrayals.

stories.title: Paul Wight expresses interest in heel turn and working with Darby Allin
stories.tldr: Paul Wight recently expressed a strong desire to turn heel and step into the ring with AEW star Darby Allin. During a virtual signing, Wight praised the incredible athleticism of the current generation of professional wrestlers. He specifically highlighted Allin as an ideal opponent for a brutal matchup that would play on their contrasting styles. Allin is currently holding his third reign as the AEW TNT Champion and preparing for upcoming defenses.

stories.title: WOL: The politics of tribute shows, Death Riders' future & confusing rules
stories.tldr: The latest early edition of the Sunday wrestling audio show hosted by Josh Nason features a heavy emphasis on All Elite Wrestling. The episode addresses the emotional fallout and tribute show following the recent passing of PAC, alongside industry conjecture regarding WWE. Additionally, the show covers Saturday's Collision, breaking down the Death Riders' future, free agents, and an incredibly confusing set of rules announced for the upcoming WrestleDream main event.

stories.title: AEW's FTR explains how they fell in love with tag team wrestling
stories.tldr: AEW stars Cash Wheeler and Dax Harwood of FTR recently shared the origins of their deep passion for tag team wrestling. Wheeler traced his love back to childhood backyard brawls with his brothers and the strategic elements of tag team psychology. Harwood reminisced about playing Saturday Night Slam Masters on the Super Nintendo with his friends, which forged a memorable bond. Together, the decorated duo has gone on to achieve historic success as multi-time champions across both WWE and AEW.

stories.title: AEW's Thunder Rosa reveals conditions to do a Blood & Guts match
stories.tldr: Former AEW Women's World Champion Thunder Rosa recently discussed the strict conditions under which she would agree to compete in another extreme stipulation match like Blood & Guts. While she is well known for her violent encounters, including her famous Lights Out match against Britt Baker, Rosa insists that future hardcore bouts must be driven by deeply meaningful storylines rather than gratuitous violence. She emphasizes that the physical toll is only worth it if the brutality genuinely serves the narrative being told in the ring. Whether she will participate in a potential future women's Blood & Guts match remains to be seen.

stories.title: Maria Kanellis talks abrupt departure from wrestling and future door
stories.tldr: Former wrestling star Maria Kanellis reflects on her abrupt departure from AEW at the end of January 2025 after a twenty-year career in the industry. Although she admits it took time to accept leaving without a proper send-off, she has since transitioned into motherhood, event management, running a florist business, and writing a book. While she is currently not involved in wrestling, she leaves the door open for a potential return if the right opportunity arises. She notes she would specifically consider a comeback if it brought her joy or allowed her to work with The Kingdom one more time.

stories.title: Cageside community reflects on memory of PAC
stories.tldr: Following the shocking and sudden passing of professional wrestler Ben PAC Satterley, the wrestling community has been left reeling once again from another tragic loss in the industry. Writers and fans alike expressed their profound grief, noting how rarely PAC broke character, especially recalling his recent emotional breakdown over the loss of Andy The Butcher Williams. In response to the tragedy, community members shared supportive comments and reflections emphasizing the importance of empathy, humanity, and unity over corporate wrestling rivalries. The resulting collection of tributes serves as a therapeutic outlet for fans processing their sorrow together.

stories.title: Young Bucks set to defend tag titles at AEW WrestleDream 2026
stories.tldr: The newly crowned four-time AEW World Tag Team Champions The Young Bucks will make their first title defense against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight of the Don Callis Family at AEW WrestleDream. Fletcher and Knight earned their championship opportunity at All Out by defeating Darby Allin and Steven Borden via referee stoppage after Borden suffered a concussion. The challengers hold strong momentum heading into the event, including a prior victory over the champions and potential dual-championship aspirations for Fletcher. Additionally, the WrestleDream card will feature major championship bouts including a Women's World Championship match and a historic Clockwork Carnage Match for the AEW World Championship.

stories.title: Big E reacts to Kofi Kingston & Austin Creed's new career path in AEW
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Big E has expressed his unwavering support for his longtime stablemates Kofi Kingston and Austin Creed following their recent move to AEW. Operating now as The New Level alongside Swerve Strickland, the duo has already captured the AEW World Trios Championships just one month into their run. Big E, who remains under WWE contract as an analyst and ambassador, emphasized that their personal bond transcends any specific company. Meanwhile, Kofi Kingston is already looking ahead to more gold as he prepares to challenge Bandido for the ROH World Championship at Grand Slam France.

stories.title: Chris Jericho reveals how he and Samoa Joe handled Tony Khan creative idea
stories.tldr: Chris Jericho recently shared insights on how he and Samoa Joe handled a creative pitch from AEW president Tony Khan that neither wrestler initially liked. Instead of rejecting the idea outright, Jericho and Joe collaborated to rework the concept into an alternative that satisfied everyone involved. Jericho emphasized that professional wrestlers should offer constructive alternatives rather than flatly refusing a boss, drawing on his extensive experience working with both Khan and Vince McMahon.

stories.title: AEW Rumor Look Back (March 27 – April 3, 2026)
stories.tldr: This weekly rumor review examines various professional wrestling reports from late March and early April 2026 to see which predictions and news items ultimately proved accurate. The retrospective evaluates claims regarding WWE events, WrestleMania 42 plans, talent injuries, and AEW scheduling shifts. Several major stories from outlets like the Wrestling Observer and various insiders are graded on their accuracy over the subsequent months.

stories.title: Swerve Strickland hopes rivalry with Hangman Page goes down as one of wrestling's greatest
stories.tldr: Swerve Strickland recently expressed his desire for his intense, multi-year feud with Hangman Page to be remembered as one of the greatest rivalries in professional wrestling history. Speaking in an interview, Strickland highlighted their unique chemistry, emotional vulnerability, and ability to captivate audiences regardless of the match stipulation. Their storied history dates back to 2023 and includes extreme encounters such as home invasions, arson, and a brutal steel cage match at All Out 2024. The two recently crossed paths again in the trios division at AEW All Out 2026, proving that fans remain intensely invested whenever they share the ring.

stories.title: Backstage Reaction To AEW All Out
stories.tldr: Backstage reaction to the 2026 AEW All Out pay-per-view was generally positive due to the strong in-ring content delivered throughout the show. However, the event was heavily overshadowed by a serious injury sustained by Steven Borden during his tag team match, which required him to be stretchered out of the arena and hospitalized. Fortunately, Borden was responsive and received positive test results following the incident. AEW now faces a rapid turnaround as they prepare for their next pay-per-view event, WrestleDream, scheduled for October 17th in Orlando, Florida.

stories.title: Eric Bischoff says AEW TV contract could limit immediate merger changes
stories.tldr: Eric Bischoff believes AEW will be insulated from immediate corporate shakeups following the upcoming Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery merger due to Tony Khan having a binding television contract. Unlike Bischoff's time running WCW as an internal Turner employee, the network cannot unilaterally pull strings without potential legal repercussions. Bischoff notes that while minor scheduling flexibility might exist depending on contract terms, Khan's budget and operational status are largely protected until the agreement nears its expiration. Consequently, any early corporate maneuvering will likely happen behind closed doors without direct visibility for AEW leadership.
